An empty table cell with the caret in it is drawn by the cell's borders, which sit on its parent. The text area inside has nothing of its own to paint, as a new table's first cell does.

A group's frame is where a person grabs the group, so it paints nothing of its own. The shapes it holds paint under it with plain fills, which the detector does not count as a sign that something is there.
The table border is its slide content. The nearby blue selection frame and handles show the selected table, so both frames are intentional.
